combo.log_composition: cb8d1b9 on top of 799d45b and 351da69 and 750ccce; integration commit 132 Pando + 799 range
combo.evidence: git diff 799d45b..cb8d1b9 touches no src/sharding files; src/sharding/migration.rs and src/sharding/sidecar.rs are byte-identical between the migration25 799 tree and the combo tree (diff --no-index empty)

verdict.summary: 799d45b fixes both open diagnostic P2s exactly as claimed. The non-200 peer branch now reads no response body at all: only the HTTP status is logged and callers receive the same static error classes, so untrusted text and the signed delegation can never reach logs or client messages (the previous truncate-before-redact defect is eliminated by deletion, not by reordering). Both 200 receipt paths use a shared collect_bounded/read_receipt helper with a hard 2048-byte cap and oversized chunks are rejected before append; the three unit tests cover unknown-length within cap, chunked overflow before append, and an oversized single chunk. The multi-hop capacity P2 is converted to a documented, deliberate fail-closed operational cap (docs: at most 1024 pin intents and 2 MiB per repository across generations; code unchanged, no quota or scalability claim). No new P1 or P2 found in the delta. Three prior P2s remain open but bounded and non-blocking. Native is only partially observed: migration25 4/4 passed on the 351 binary (so the prior 351-pending statement is historical), while the combo cb8d1b9 build is 3/4 with partition still running; the fe8 hook worker with 5 unexercised hooks is not qualified, the old takeover generic 409 remains unclassified, and physical cross-host is unqualified. #25 stays OPEN.

closed_in_this_delta.evidence: migration.rs:111-134: on non-200 the response body is never read or parsed; the only output is eprintln target_status=<StatusCode> and static class errors. No delegation variable, no peer text, no redaction dependency.

migration.rs:64-88 collect_bounded/read_receipt; 137 SnapshotReceipt and 160 FinalizeReceipt both use read_receipt with MAX_RECEIPT_BYTES=2048; each chunk is rejected with replica receipt too large before append when it would exceed the remaining cap; stream errors map to static 502.

docs/cluster-local-process-fence.md states the fixed 1024-intent/2 MiB per-repository cap including historical generations is a deliberate fail-closed operational limit, not a capacity/scalability claim; code unchanged.

findings.title: handoff_pending checks only receipt existence; lost live evidence re-opens the old 409 unmanaged path and corrupt/missing staging becomes an indistinguishable permanent 503
findings.bound: Non-blocking: fail-closed, no silent authorization or data loss; requires operator-visible stuck state only after live-directory loss or staging corruption.
findings.trigger: Delete/restore ci-pins/<repo> after a publication receipt exists -> fresh pin 409 unmanaged; or delete staging for a completed op with no receipt -> every pin gets permanent 503 CI sidecar handoff pending.

findings.title: Receipt replay rejects a legitimate release followed by a re-pin of the same job id
findings.bound: Non-blocking: only affects replay/startup verification after release+re-pin; publication data is correct.
findings.trigger: Publish migration, release job J, re-pin job J with a new oid, restart target -> 409 published CI sidecar file is missing.

findings.title: Orphan staging with no operation row is retained forever with no quarantine or audit signal
findings.bound: Non-blocking: deliberate retain-on-unknown (no data loss), causes unbounded disk growth and no operator signal.
findings.trigger: Copy a stale <uuid>.sidecar staging dir with no operation row into shard-staging and restart the target: retained forever, nothing reported.

new_observations_non_blocking: read_receipt maps a malformed or empty 200 receipt body to Error::internal (500) rather than a peer-fault 502; same as the previous behavior, observability nit only (migration.rs:84-87).

The three unit tests validate collect_bounded only; they do not deserialize SnapshotReceipt/FinalizeReceipt nor exercise the non-200 no-read branch. Cargo check/unit pass is accepted as supplied, not reproduced here.
The non-200 branch returns without draining the peer body; the response is dropped, so a large error body cannot be accumulated, but the connection is not reused. No security or memory issue.
transport.rs:317 still streams forwarded Git output with the existing max_output_bytes accounting; it is outside this receipt-read delta and unchanged.
